payload.text: Stability of the noise, not presence of it, decides gradeability; the repeat count is FLAT across every slide; and where a floor's structure is known it is a derived CEILING rather than a largest-observed value. MEASURED 2026-09-09, thirty captures of slide 14 by hash: THREE renders -- A=21 (0.700), B=8 (0.267), C=1 (0.033) -- so P(miss)=sum(p_i^n) is 56.2 percent at n=2, 16.9 at n=5, under 5 percent first at n=9 and under 1 percent at n=13. Thirteen captures per slide. AN ADAPTIVE PER-SLIDE COUNT IS REFUSED and this row said the opposite until it was measured: deciding a slide is stable requires the same evidence as proving it is, so escalating only the slides that look unstable under-detects exactly those that need it. THE TAIL IS CLOSED STRUCTURALLY, NOT SAMPLED: all three renders differ only at the two ENDPOINTS of one 59-pixel edge at x=145, so the renders are (top,bottom) with each end rounding independently -- A=(0,0), C=(0,1), B=(1,1), and a predicted D=(1,0). The maximum possible difference is both endpoints flipping, which IS A-to-B, so 0.002196 is a ceiling no unobserved mode can exceed. Confirmed independently by magnitude as well as geometry: RMSE(A,B)/RMSE(A,C) = 1.41404 against sqrt(2) = 1.41421, which is what 4 differing pixels against 2 of equal delta predicts.
